subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: Should OpenClaw fix this by changing the default channel delivery contract for intermediate assistant text, or by adding an opt-in final-only/suppress-interim mode while preserving automatic bare-text replies by default?
rationale: Current tests and source preserve automatic/multi-segment delivery in some paths, but the issue is also a security and channel-trust problem; automation cannot choose the compatibility break versus opt-in safety policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add Upgrade-Safe Suppression Mode
options.body: Add a shared final-only or suppress-interim policy at payload construction with a clear default/migration story, then consider a later default flip once operators have an escape hatch.

options.title: Flip External Channels To Explicit Sends
options.body: Make external channel replies message-tool-only or final-only by default, accepting compatibility risk for users relying on bare assistant text delivery.

options.title: Keep Automatic Defaults
options.body: Leave automatic delivery as the default and document existing `message_tool_only` or prompt-based workarounds, accepting that the reported leak class remains possible.

recommendation.title: Add Upgrade-Safe Suppression Mode
recommendation.body: Add a shared final-only or suppress-interim policy at payload construction with a clear default/migration story, then consider a later default flip once operators have an escape hatch.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main routing signal is recent ownership of the payload fallback, phased text, and source-reply policy surfaces.
